title: CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Anne's Life

paragraphs.en: Anne was walking back with the cows through Lover’s Lane on a September evening. The sunset light bathed the woods in a ruby glow, but the lane itself was already shadowy under the maples and violet-dappled beneath the firs. The wind rustled through the fir trees, creating a sweet melody.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮在九月的一个傍晚，带着奶牛走在情人谷里。夕阳的余晖将树林染成了红宝石般的色彩，但小径本身已在枫树的阴影中变得幽暗，还因松树下散布着紫色的斑点而显得更加神秘。风穿过松树，发出悦耳的沙沙声，仿佛在低吟浅唱。

paragraphs.en: The cows moved slowly down the path, and Anne recited aloud from Marmion, feeling the rush of the battle imagery. She paused at the lines about the spearsmen, closing her eyes to imagine herself among them.
paragraphs.zh: 奶牛缓缓沿着小路走下，安妮出声吟诵着《马米翁》中的诗句，感受着战斗场面的激昂。她停在描述长矛兵的那几行诗前，闭上眼睛想象自己置身其中。

paragraphs.en: Diana appeared at the gate leading into Barry field, looking important. Anne sensed there was news but held back her curiosity. "Isn't this evening beautiful?
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜出现在通往巴里田地的小门边，显得神采奕奕。安妮感觉到她要宣布什么消息，但还是忍住了好奇心。“今夜的景色多美啊！”

paragraphs.en: It makes me so glad to be alive."
paragraphs.zh: 活着真是让我如此高兴。

paragraphs.en: "It is a fine evening," Diana replied, "but I have something to tell you. Guess—three guesses!"
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜回答说：“这是一个美好的夜晚，但我有件事要告诉你。猜一猜——给你三次机会！”

paragraphs.en: "Is Charlotte Gillis getting married in the church after all?" Anne guessed.
paragraphs.zh: “查尔斯敦·吉利斯究竟是否会在教堂举行婚礼呢？”安妮猜道。

paragraphs.en: "No, her beau won’t agree because it would look too much like a funeral. It’s not fun at all. Try again."
paragraphs.zh: “不，她的 boyfriend 不会同意的，因为这未免太像葬礼了。根本没什么意思。再试一次吧。”

paragraphs.en: "Is Jane having a birthday party?"
paragraphs.zh: “简在开生日派对吗？”

paragraphs.en: Diana shook her head, laughing. "It's something else entirely. Did Moody Spurgeon MacPherson see you home from prayer meeting last night?"
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜摇了摇头，笑着说道：“这完全不是一回事。莫迪·斯潘塞·麦菲森昨晚从祷告会送你回家了吗？”

paragraphs.en: Diana exclaimed indignantly, "I should think not." "If he did boast of it, that horrid creature wouldn't," she continued. "Mother received a letter from Aunt Josephine today, inviting us to town next Tuesday for the Exhibition."
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜愤愤不平地喊道：“我才不信呢。”她继续说道：“如果他敢吹嘘的话，那个可恶的东西肯定不会承认的。”接着说，“妈妈今天收到了乔斯林姑妈的来信，邀请我们下周二去镇上参加展览。”

paragraphs.en: Anne leaned against a maple tree, whispering, "Oh, Diana, do you really mean it? I'm afraid Marilla won't let me go. She said last week that she couldn't encourage gadding about when Jane invited me to the American concert at White Sands Hotel.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮靠在一棵枫树上，轻声说道：“戴安娜，你真的这么想吗？我怕玛丽拉不会让我去。她上周说，当简邀请我去白沙滩酒店的美国音乐会时，她不能鼓励我到处乱跑。”

paragraphs.en: I wanted to go but was told to stay home and learn my lessons."
paragraphs.zh: 我想去，却被要求留在家里好好学习。

paragraphs.en: Diana replied, "We'll get Mother to ask Marilla. If she agrees, we'll have a great time. I've never been to an Exhibition, and it's so annoying to hear other girls talk about their trips.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜回答说：“我们去找妈妈问问玛丽拉。如果她答应了，那可真是件大事。我从未去过展览会，每次听别的女孩谈论她们的旅行都感到挺烦人。”

paragraphs.en: Jane and Ruby went twice, and they're going again this year."
paragraphs.zh: 简和ruby已经去了两次，今年还要再去一次。

paragraphs.en: Anne decided not to think about going to town until she knew if it was possible. She feared being disappointed would be too much to handle. However, if she did go, she was glad her new coat would be ready by then.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮决定，在确切知道是否可行之前，不要考虑进城的事。她担心受挫的情绪自己难以承受。不过，如果真的出行，她很高兴新外套届时已经准备好了。

paragraphs.en: Marilla had initially thought Anne didn't need a new coat, suggesting the old one could last another winter. But Matthew insisted on a new coat, and Marilla bought blue broadcloth for a dressmaker in Carmody to make it. The coat was due to be completed on Saturday night.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉最初以为安妮不需要新外套，建议旧的还能再穿一个冬天。但马修坚持要给安妮买件新的，于是玛丽拉在卡姆多伊找裁缝定做了件蓝色哔叽料的新外套。这件外套预计将在星期六晚上做好。

paragraphs.en: Anne couldn’t help imagining herself walking up the church aisle on Sunday in her new suit and cap. Her cap was particularly pretty; Matthew had bought it for her during their visit to Carmody. It was one of those fashionable little blue velvet caps with gold cords and tassels.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮不禁想象自己在周日穿着新衣服和帽子走上教堂过道的情景。她的帽子尤其漂亮；马修在他们去卡姆多伊的访问期间给她买的。那是一顶时尚的小蓝绒帽，配有金色的丝带和流苏。

paragraphs.en: Anne felt proud when she saw Diana’s elegant new hat at church last Sunday.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮在上周日的教堂里看到戴安娜那顶优雅的新帽子时，感到十分自豪。

paragraphs.en: Marilla believed thinking about clothes was sinful, but Anne found the subject interesting. Marilla agreed to let Anne go to town, and Mr. Barry would take them on Tuesday. The journey was thirty miles away, so they had to leave very early.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉认为思考衣服的事是罪过的，但安妮觉得这个话题挺有趣的。玛丽拉同意让安妮去镇上一趟，巴里先生会在星期二带她们去。这段旅程有三十英里远，所以她们不得不早早出发。

paragraphs.en: Despite this, Anne was excited and woke up before sunrise on Tuesday morning.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管如此，安妮还是兴奋不已，星期二清晨还没破晓就醒了。

paragraphs.en: Looking out her window, she saw a clear sky behind the fir trees of Haunted Wood, silvery and cloudless. Through the gap in the trees, she noticed Diana’s light was also on, indicating that her friend had risen early as well.
paragraphs.zh: 透过窗户，她看到Haunted Wood松树林后方的天空一片清澈，银光闪烁，没有一丝云彩。透过树间的缝隙，她注意到戴安娜家的灯光也亮着，看来好友也早早起床了。

paragraphs.en: Anne had dressed by the time Matthew started the fire and prepared breakfast for Marilla. Despite being excited, she couldn't eat much. After breakfast, Anne put on a new jaunty cap and jacket and rushed across the brook to Orchard Slope with Diana and Mr. Barry.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮在马修生火和为玛丽拉准备早餐之前就已经穿好了衣服。尽管她心情激动，却吃得不多。吃过早饭后，安妮戴上一顶新买的俏皮帽子和夹克，匆匆穿过小溪，与戴安娜和巴里先生一起前往果园坡。

paragraphs.en: The drive was long but enjoyable. They rattled along the moist roads under early red sunlight, passing through fields of harvested crops. The air was fresh, and blue mists curled through valleys and floated from hills.
paragraphs.zh: 驾车路程虽长但十分愉快。他们在初升的红日下沿着湿润的道路颠簸前行，穿过一片片收割后的田地。空气清新宜人，蓝色的雾气在山谷间缭绕，在山丘上飘浮。

paragraphs.en: Sometimes they drove through woods where maples displayed vibrant scarlet leaves; other times, they crossed rivers on bridges that made Anne's skin prickle with old fear. They also passed fishing huts by the harbor shore and climbed hills offering views of distant uplands or misty skies.
paragraphs.zh: 有时他们穿行在枫树映衬出绚烂红叶的森林中；有时则要过河，桥上斑驳的记忆让安妮不禁感到一丝久远的恐惧。沿途还有渔舍点缀着海港岸边，登上山坡又能俯瞰远处连绵的高地或是雾气蒙蒙的天空。

paragraphs.en: By noon, they reached town and found their way to "Beechwood," a fine old mansion set back from the street among green elms and beeches. Miss Barry greeted them with a twinkle in her sharp black eyes.
paragraphs.zh: 到中午时分，他们来到了镇上，并找到了“橡树庄”——这是一座古朴而典雅的老宅，坐落在绿荫掩映的街道后方，周围是郁郁葱葱的榆树和山毛榉。巴里小姐用她那双锐利的黑眼睛中闪烁的光芒迎接了他们。

paragraphs.en: "So you've finally come to see me, Anne-girl," she said. "Mercy, child, how you’ve grown! You’re taller than I am.
paragraphs.zh: “你终于来看我了，安妮姑娘，”她说道，“天啊，孩子，你可真是长大了不少！你现在都比我高了。

paragraphs.en: And much prettier too, though I’m sure you know that."
paragraphs.zh: 而且肯定更加漂亮，尽管你心里有数。

paragraphs.en: Anne beamed, saying, "I didn't realize it until now. I knew my freckles had faded, but I hadn’t hoped for any other changes. I'm so glad you think there is improvement."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮脸上洋溢着笑容，说道：“直到现在我才意识到这一点。我知道我的雀斑淡了，但没想到会有其他的变化。我很高兴你认为有所改善。”

paragraphs.en: Inside Miss Barry's magnificently furnished parlor, Anne and Diana felt somewhat overwhelmed.
paragraphs.zh: 在巴里小姐那装饰华丽的客厅里，安妮和戴安娜感到有些不知所措。

paragraphs.en: "Isn't this like a palace?" whispered Diana. "I've never been to Aunt Josephine’s house before, and it’s much grander than I imagined.
paragraphs.zh: “这不是皇宫吗？”戴安娜低声说道，“我以前从没去过乔斯林姑妈家，没想到竟然如此气派。”

paragraphs.en: Julia Bell would be amazed if she saw this—she always talks about her mother's parlor with such pride."
paragraphs.zh: 朱莉娅·贝尔如果看到这番景象肯定会大吃一惊——她总是如此自豪地谈论她母亲的客厅。

paragraphs.en: Anne sighed, "Velvet carpet and silk curtains! I dreamed of such things, Diana. But after all, they don't feel as comfortable as I imagined."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮叹了口气，“天鹅绒地毯和丝绸窗帘！戴安娜，我曾梦想过这些东西。但毕竟，它们并没有像想象中那样让人感到舒适。”

paragraphs.en: The visit to town remained a cherished memory for Anne and Diana. Miss Barry took them to the Exhibition grounds on Wednesday, keeping them there all day.
paragraphs.zh: 镇上的参观成了安妮和戴安娜心中珍贵的记忆。巴里小姐在星期三带她们去了展览会现场，并在那里整整待了一整天。

paragraphs.en: Despite the splendor, Anne found little room for imagination in the many splendid items in the room.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管房间里摆放着许多华丽的物品，安妮却发现自己很难在这些辉煌的事物中发挥丰富的想象力。

paragraphs.en: Anne recounted her experience at the fair to Marilla later. "It was splendid," she said with enthusiasm. "I never imagined anything so interesting.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮后来向玛丽拉讲述了她在集市上的经历。“真是太精彩了，”她充满热情地说，“我从没想过会有如此有趣的事情。”

paragraphs.en: I think I liked the horses, flowers, and fancywork best." Josie Pye won first prize for knitted lace, which made Anne happy. Mr. Harmon Andrews took second prize for Gravenstein apples, while Mr. Bell won first prize for a pig.
paragraphs.zh: 我想我最喜欢的是马匹、鲜花和手工艺品。乔西·皮伊编织的花边获得了第一名，这让安妮感到很高兴。汉蒙·安德鲁斯先生因种植格伦斯坦苹果获得第二名，而贝尔先生则因一头猪赢得了第一名。

paragraphs.en: Diana thought it ridiculous for a Sunday-school superintendent to win in pigs, but Anne didn't see why not. Clara Louise MacPherson got a prize for painting, and Mrs. Lynde won first prize for homemade butter and cheese. Avonlea was well-represented at the fair.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜觉得周日学校管理者的养猪比赛获胜未免有些荒谬，但安妮却不以为然。克拉拉·路易丝·麦克弗森因为绘画获得了奖品，而林德太太则凭借自制黄油和奶酪赢得了头等奖。埃文利镇在此次博览会上表现得相当出色。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Lynde attended, and seeing her familiar face among strangers made Anne feel insignificant.
paragraphs.zh: 莉nde太太也来了，她的熟悉面孔出现在陌生人之中让安妮感到自己有些微不足道。

paragraphs.en: Miss Barry took them to the grandstand to watch horse races, while Mrs. Lynde stayed away because she considered it an abomination. Diana got so excited that she offered to bet ten cents on the red horse winning. Anne refused, wanting to tell Mrs. Allan about everything and avoiding any indiscretion.
paragraphs.zh: 巴里小姐带她们去了看马术比赛的看台，而雷切尔·林德夫人则避开了那里，认为那是一种罪恶。戴安娜兴奋得不得了，竟然提出要打赌十美分，押注红马能赢。安妮婉拒了她的提议，一心想要把所有事情都告诉艾伦太太，并且不想有任何不当之举。

paragraphs.en: They saw a man go up in a balloon, which thrilled Anne, and watched a fortune-teller who picked fortunes for ten cents. Miss Barry gave them each ten cents to have their fortunes told. Anne's was that she would marry a wealthy dark-complected man and live across the water.
paragraphs.zh: 他们目睹了一位男子乘坐热气球升空，这让安妮兴奋不已。接着，她们还围观了一个算命师，每人花十美分抽取命运签。巴里小姐给了每个人十美分让他们抽签看命运。轮到安妮时，她的签上写道：她将会嫁给一位富有且肤色较深的男子，并生活在对面的岛上。

paragraphs.en: She didn't find any of the dark men appealing.
paragraphs.zh: 她对那些皮肤黝黑的男子并没有什么好感。

paragraphs.en: The day left an indelible impression on Anne, making her tired but happy. Miss Barry put them in the spare room as promised, which turned out to be less exciting than expected. Anne realized that growing up had its drawbacks, as childhood dreams seemed less wonderful when they came true.
paragraphs.zh: 这一天给安妮留下了深刻的印象，让她感到既疲惫又快乐。巴里小姐如承诺般将她们安置在了备用房间，结果却比预期的要平淡无奇得多。安妮意识到，成长并非总是美好之事，当儿时的梦想一一实现时，它们似乎也没有当初想象中那么令人向往。

paragraphs.en: On Thursday, Anne and her friends went on a drive in the park. In the evening, they attended a concert at the Academy of Music where Madame Selitsky performed. The experience was overwhelming for Anne.
paragraphs.zh: 星期四，安妮和她的朋友们去公园兜风。晚上，她们在音乐学院听了塞利茨基夫人的音乐会演出。这次经历让安妮感到震撼不已。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla, it was beyond description," she exclaimed. "I sat in silent awe as Madame Selitsky sang. Her beauty and the music moved me deeply."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，玛丽拉，那简直无法用言语形容，”她脱口而出。“我静静地聆听着赛利斯基夫人唱歌，她的美丽和音乐深深打动了我。”

paragraphs.en: The next morning, Miss Barry suggested they have ice cream at a nearby restaurant to help Anne return to reality. To Anne's surprise, the experience was delightful.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天早上，巴里小姐建议她们去附近的一家餐馆吃冰淇淋，帮助安妮回到现实。令安妮惊讶的是，这次经历非常愉快。

paragraphs.en: "Marilla, it was so lovely to eat ice cream at eleven o'clock," she said. "But I realized that city life wasn't for me. I preferred being in the east gable, asleep but aware of the stars and the wind outside."
paragraphs.zh: “玛丽拉，能在十一点钟吃冰淇淋真是太美妙了，”她说，“但我也意识到城市生活不适合我。我喜欢在东屋睡觉，虽然睡着了，但仍能感受到外面的星光和微风。”

paragraphs.en: At breakfast, Miss Barry laughed at Anne's reflections, which made her feel a bit uncomfortable.
paragraphs.zh: 在早餐时，巴里小姐笑谈着安妮的沉思，这让安妮感到有些不自在。

paragraphs.en: "Well, I hope you've enjoyed yourselves," Miss Barry said as she bid them farewell on Friday morning.
paragraphs.zh: 巴里小姐在星期五早上告别他们时说道：“玩得开心吗？”

paragraphs.en: Anne and Diana returned home from their drive with renewed joy. The sunset painted the Avonlea hills in dark silhouettes against the saffron sky as they passed through White Sands. The moon rose over the radiant sea, casting a magical light on every cove along the curving road.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮和戴安娜驱车回家时心情更加愉悦了。夕阳将埃文利的山峦勾勒成深色剪影，映衬在金黄色的天幕之下，两人途经白沙滩时，景色尤为美丽。月亮从波光粼粼的大海上冉冉升起，为蜿蜒的道路旁每一个海湾洒下了一抹神奇的光芒。

paragraphs.en: "Isn't it wonderful to be alive and going home?" Anne exclaimed.
paragraphs.zh: “活着并回家，多美妙啊！”安妮兴奋地喊道。

paragraphs.en: Upon crossing the log bridge, the kitchen light of Green Gables greeted them warmly. Inside, Marilla was knitting, but she paused as Anne ran up the hill into the kitchen where a warm supper awaited.
paragraphs.zh: 跨过木桥后，绿山墙农舍的厨房灯光热情地迎接了他们。屋内，玛丽拉正在织毛衣，但当安妮飞奔上山，跑到厨房时，她停下了手中的活儿。餐桌上摆着一顿温馨的晚餐，在等待着她们的到来。

paragraphs.en: "So you've got back," Marilla said, folding her knitting.
paragraphs.zh: “你终于回来了，”玛丽拉说着，收起了手中的针线活。

paragraphs.en: Anne returned with joy: "Yes, and oh, it's so good to be back." She exclaimed, "I could kiss everything, even the clock. Marilla, a broiled chicken!
paragraphs.zh: 安妮欢天喜地地回来了：“是的，而且啊，回家的感觉真是太好了。”她激动地说，“我简直想亲吻一切，就连那只钟都想亲一口。玛丽拉，今晚有烤鸡！

paragraphs.en: You cooked that for me?"
paragraphs.zh: “你给我做的这个？”

paragraphs.en: "Yes, I did," replied Marilla. "I thought you'd be hungry after your drive and needed something appetizing."
paragraphs.zh: “是的，我是这么想的。”玛丽拉回答，“我觉得你刚兜了一圈车肯定饿了，需要点开胃的食物。”

paragraphs.en: After supper, Anne sat between Matthew and Marilla by the fire. She recounted her visit happily: "I've had a splendid time, and this marks an epoch in my life. The best part was coming home."
paragraphs.zh: 吃过晚饭后，安妮坐在壁炉旁的马修和玛丽拉中间。她高兴地回忆起这次访问：“我玩得非常开心，这在我的生活中是一个重要的转折点。最让人兴奋的是回到家。”
